PerfectSequencer

Frame-accurate event scheduling for Roblox
npm package →

![GitHub Workflow Status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/skatingii/PerfectSequencer/ci.yml?style=for-the-badge&branch=main&logo=github) [![NPM Version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@skating/perfect-sequencer.svg?style=for-the-badge&logo=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@skating/perfect-sequencer) [![GitHub License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/skatingii/PerfectSequencer?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE)
PerfectSequencer schedules callbacks by animation frame instead of by seconds. Write `12` and mean frame 12, the same number an animator reads off the timeline, rather than translating it into `task.wait(0.2)` and hoping the two stay in step. **Two schedulers, for two different problems:** - Fire events on a [shared clock](#addeventevent) that ticks against real `DeltaTime`, so timings hold under frame drops - Fire events on an [animation's own timeline](#fortracktrack), so they follow the track through speed changes and die with it **Why frames instead of seconds?** Animation data is authored in frames. Once a hitbox is written as `0.2` seconds, the link back to the keyframe it came from is gone, and retiming the animation silently desynchronises the gameplay. Keeping the frame number keeps that link.
Table of Contents - [Installation](#installation) - [At a Glance](#at-a-glance) - [Reference](#reference) - [`AddEvent(Event)`](#addeventevent) - [`Run()`](#run) - [`Stop()`](#stop) - [`Reset()`](#reset) - [`IsRunning()`](#isrunning) - [`GetPendingCount()`](#getpendingcount) - [`Completed`](#completed) - [`ForTrack(Track)`](#fortracktrack) - [`TrackSequencer:At(Frame, Callback, Args?)`](#tracksequenceratframe-callback-args) - [`TrackSequencer:Start()`](#tracksequencerstart) - [`TrackSequencer:Cancel()`](#tracksequencercancel) - [`TrackSequencer.Finished`](#tracksequencerfinished) - [Choosing a scheduler](#choosing-a-scheduler) - [Compared to animation markers](#compared-to-animation-markers) - [Edge cases](#edge-cases) - [How it behaves](#how-it-behaves) - [Contributing](#contributing)
## Installation **Luau, with [Wally](https://wally.run):** ```toml # wally.toml [dependencies] PerfectSequencer = "skatingii/perfect-sequencer@0.1.0" ``` Then run `wally install`. The package lands at `Packages/PerfectSequencer`. **TypeScript, with [roblox-ts](https://roblox-ts.com):** ```bash npm install @skating/perfect-sequencer ``` ```ts import PerfectSequencer from "@skating/perfect-sequencer"; ``` The two registries use different scopes because they key off different accounts: Wally uses the GitHub username, npm uses the npm usern

--!strict

export type Task = any

type Fields = {
	Tasks: { Task },
}

const Cleanup = {}
Cleanup.__index = Cleanup

export type Cleanup = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, Cleanup))

function Cleanup.new(): Cleanup
	const self: Fields = {
		Tasks = {},
	}

	return setmetatable(self, Cleanup)
end

function Cleanup.Add(self: Cleanup, Item: Task): Task
	table.insert(self.Tasks, Item)

	return Item
end

function Cleanup.Clean(self: Cleanup)
	const Pending = self.Tasks
	self.Tasks = {}

	for _, Item in Pending do
		const Kind = typeof(Item)

		if Kind == "RBXScriptConnection" then
			Item:Disconnect()
		elseif Kind == "Instance" then
			Item:Destroy()
		elseif Kind == "function" then
			Item()
		elseif Kind == "thread" then
			const Succeeded = pcall(task.cancel, Item)

			if not Succeeded then
				warn("[perfect sequencer] could not cancel a pending thread, it may already be running")
			end
		elseif Kind == "table" then
			if Item.Disconnect then
				Item:Disconnect()
			elseif Item.Destroy then
				Item:Destroy()
			else
				warn("[perfect sequencer] a table was given to Cleanup with no Disconnect or Destroy method")
			end
		else
			warn(`[perfect sequencer] Cleanup does not know how to clean a {Kind}`)
		end
	end

	table.clear(Pending)
end

Cleanup.Destroy = Cleanup.Clean

return Cleanup

--!strict

export type Event = {
	TargetFrame: number,
	Callback: (...any) -> ...any,
	Args: { any }?,
}

const Queue = {}

function Queue.Insert(Events: { Event }, Item: Event)
	local Low, High = 1, #Events + 1

	while Low < High do
		const Middle = (Low + High) // 2

		if Events[Middle].TargetFrame > Item.TargetFrame then
			Low = Middle + 1
		else
			High = Middle
		end
	end

	table.insert(Events, Low, Item)
end

function Queue.TakeDue(Events: { Event }, Clock: number): { Event }
	const Due: { Event } = {}

	for Index = #Events, 1, -1 do
		const Item = Events[Index]

		if Clock < Item.TargetFrame then
			break
		end

		table.remove(Events, Index)
		table.insert(Due, Item)
	end

	return Due
end

return Queue

--!strict

export type Connection = {
	Connected: boolean,
	Handler: (...any) -> (),
	Next: Connection?,
	Disconnect: (self: Connection) -> (),
}

type Fields = {
	Head: Connection?,
}

local FreeRunnerThread: thread? = nil

const function AcquireRunnerThreadAndCallHandler(Handler: (...any) -> (), ...: any)
	const AcquiredThread = FreeRunnerThread
	FreeRunnerThread = nil

	Handler(...)

	FreeRunnerThread = AcquiredThread
end

const function RunHandlerInFreeThread(...: any)
	AcquireRunnerThreadAndCallHandler(...)

	while true do
		AcquireRunnerThreadAndCallHandler(coroutine.yield())
	end
end

const SignalClass = {}
SignalClass.__index = SignalClass

export type Signal = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, SignalClass))

function SignalClass.Connect(self: Signal, Handler: (...any) -> ()): Connection
	const Link: Connection = {
		Connected = true,
		Handler = Handler,
		Next = self.Head,

		Disconnect = function(Node: Connection)
			if not Node.Connected then
				return
			end

			Node.Connected = false

			if self.Head == Node then
				self.Head = Node.Next
				return
			end

			local Previous = self.Head

			while Previous and Previous.Next ~= Node do
				Previous = Previous.Next
			end

			if Previous then
				Previous.Next = Node.Next
			end
		end,
	}

	self.Head = Link

	return Link
end

function SignalClass.Once(self: Signal, Handler: (...any) -> ()): Connection
	local Link: Connection

	Link = self:Connect(function(...)
		Link:Disconnect()
		Handler(...)
	end)

	return Link
end

function SignalClass.Wait(self: Signal): ...any
	const Waiting = coroutine.running()

	self:Once(function(...)
		task.spawn(Waiting, ...)
	end)

	return coroutine.yield()
end

function SignalClass.Fire(self: Signal, ...: any)
	local Link = self.Head

	while Link do
		if Link.Connected then
			local Runner = FreeRunnerThread

			if not Runner then
				Runner = coroutine.create(RunHandlerInFreeThread)
				FreeRunnerThread = Runner
			end

			if Runner then
				task.spawn(Runner, Link.Handler, ...)
			end
		end

		Link = Link.Next
	end
end

function SignalClass.DisconnectAll(self: Signal)
	local Link = self.Head

	while Link do
		Link.Connected = false
		Link = Link.Next
	end

	self.Head = nil
end

SignalClass.Destroy = SignalClass.DisconnectAll

const Signal = {}

function Signal.new(): Signal
	const self: Fields = {
		Head = nil,
	}

	return setmetatable(self, SignalClass)
end

return Signal

--!strict

const RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

const Signal = require("./Signal")
const Cleanup = require("./Cleanup")
const Dispatcher = require("./Dispatcher")
const Queue = require("./Queue")
const TrackState = require("./TrackState")

const TRACING = RunService:IsStudio()

export type ScheduledEvent = Queue.Event

type Fields = {
	Track: AnimationTrack,
	State: TrackState.State,
	Cleanup: Cleanup.Cleanup,
	Finished: Signal.Signal,
	IsDead: boolean,
	HasStarted: boolean,
}

const TrackSequencer = {}
TrackSequencer.__index = TrackSequencer

export type TrackSequencer = typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, TrackSequencer))

function TrackSequencer.new(Track: AnimationTrack): TrackSequencer
	const self: Fields = {
		Track = Track,
		State = TrackState.new(os.clock()),
		Cleanup = Cleanup.new(),
		Finished = Signal.new(),
		IsDead = false,
		HasStarted = false,
	}

	return setmetatable(self, TrackSequencer)
end

function TrackSequencer.At(
	self: TrackSequencer,
	Frame: number,
	Callback: Dispatcher.Callback,
	Args: { any }?
): TrackSequencer
	if self.IsDead then
		warn(`[perfect sequencer] :At({Frame}) ignored, this track sequencer already finished`)
		return self
	end

	TrackState.Add(self.State, {
		TargetFrame = Frame,
		Callback = Callback,
		Args = Args,
	})

	return self
end

function TrackSequencer.Cancel(self: TrackSequencer)
	if self.IsDead then
		return
	end

	self.IsDead = true
	self.Cleanup:Clean()

	const Unfired = #self.State.Events
	table.clear(self.State.Events)

	self.Finished:Fire(Unfired == 0)
	self.Finished:Destroy()
end

function TrackSequencer.Start(self: TrackSequencer): TrackSequencer
	if self.IsDead or self.HasStarted then
		return self
	end

	self.HasStarted = true

	self.Cleanup:Add(RunService.PostSimulation:Connect(function()
		if self.IsDead then
			return
		end

		const Result = TrackState.Step(self.State, self.Track.IsPlaying, self.Track.TimePosition, os.clock())

		for _, Event in Result.Due do
			Dispatcher.Dispatch(Event.Callback, Event.Args)
		end

		if Result.TimedOut and TRACING then
			warn(`[perfect sequencer] track "{self.Track.Name}" never played, cancelling`)
		end

		if Result.Cancel then
			self:Cancel()
		end
	end))

	return self
end

return TrackSequencer

--!strict

const Queue = require("./Queue")

const FRAMES_PER_SECOND = 60
const NEVER_PLAYED_TIMEOUT = 1

export type State = {
	Events: { Queue.Event },
	HasPlayed: boolean,
	StartedAt: number,
}

export type Step = {
	Due: { Queue.Event },
	Cancel: boolean,
	TimedOut: boolean,
}

const TrackState = {}

function TrackState.new(StartedAt: number): State
	return {
		Events = {},
		HasPlayed = false,
		StartedAt = StartedAt,
	}
end

function TrackState.Add(self: State, Event: Queue.Event)
	table.insert(self.Events, Event)
end

function TrackState.Step(self: State, IsPlaying: boolean, TimePosition: number, Now: number): Step
	if not IsPlaying then
		if not self.HasPlayed and Now - self.StartedAt <= NEVER_PLAYED_TIMEOUT then
			return { Due = {}, Cancel = false, TimedOut = false }
		end

		return { Due = {}, Cancel = true, TimedOut = not self.HasPlayed }
	end

	self.HasPlayed = true

	const Frame = TimePosition * FRAMES_PER_SECOND
	const Due: { Queue.Event } = {}

	for Index = #self.Events, 1, -1 do
		const Event = self.Events[Index]

		if Frame >= Event.TargetFrame then
			table.remove(self.Events, Index)
			table.insert(Due, Event)
		end
	end

	table.sort(Due, function(Left, Right)
		return Left.TargetFrame < Right.TargetFrame
	end)

	return { Due = Due, Cancel = #self.Events == 0, TimedOut = false }
end

return TrackState

--[[

	PerfectSequencer
	Made by skaterstudios

	Frame-accurate event scheduling for Roblox.

	AddEvent and Run share one wall-clock scheduler whose delays are measured
	in 60fps frames but ticked against real DeltaTime, so they hold under
	frame drops.

	ForTrack returns a per-swing scheduler locked to an AnimationTrack's own
	timeline. It follows the animation through speed changes and dies with
	the track.

	Version 0.1.0

]]

--!strict

const RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

const Signal = require("@self/Signal")
const Cleanup = require("@self/Cleanup")
const Dispatcher = require("@self/Dispatcher")
const Queue = require("@self/Queue")
const TrackSequencer = require("@self/TrackSequencer")

const FRAMES_PER_SECOND = 60

export type SequencerEvent = {
	PresetFrame: number,
	Callback: Dispatcher.Callback,
	Args: { any }?,
}

export type TrackSequencer = TrackSequencer.TrackSequencer

const PerfectSequencer = {}

PerfectSequencer.Completed = Signal.new()

const Events: { Queue.Event } = {}
local RunCleanup: Cleanup.Cleanup? = nil
local Clock = 0

function PerfectSequencer.AddEvent(Event: SequencerEvent)
	if type(Event.PresetFrame) ~= "number" then
		warn(`[perfect sequencer] AddEvent needs a numeric PresetFrame, got {typeof(Event.PresetFrame)}`)
		return
	end

	if type(Event.Callback) ~= "function" then
		warn(`[perfect sequencer] AddEvent needs a Callback function, got {typeof(Event.Callback)}`)
		return
	end

	const Base = if RunCleanup then Clock else 0

	Queue.Insert(Events, {
		TargetFrame = Base + Event.PresetFrame,
		Callback = Event.Callback,
		Args = Event.Args,
	})
end

function PerfectSequencer.Reset()
	table.clear(Events)
end

function PerfectSequencer.IsRunning(): boolean
	return RunCleanup ~= nil
end

function PerfectSequencer.GetPendingCount(): number
	return #Events
end

function PerfectSequencer.Stop()
	if not RunCleanup then
		return
	end

	RunCleanup:Clean()
	RunCleanup = nil

	PerfectSequencer.Completed:Fire()
end

function PerfectSequencer.Run()
	if RunCleanup then
		return
	end

	Clock = 0

	const NewCleanup = Cleanup.new()
	RunCleanup = NewCleanup

	NewCleanup:Add(RunService.PostSimulation:Connect(function(DeltaTime: number)
		Clock += DeltaTime * FRAMES_PER_SECOND

		for _, Item in Queue.TakeDue(Events, Clock) do
			Dispatcher.Dispatch(Item.Callback, Item.Args)
		end

		if #Events == 0 then
			PerfectSequencer.Stop()
		end
	end))
end

function PerfectSequencer.ForTrack(Track: AnimationTrack): TrackSequencer.TrackSequencer
	return TrackSequencer.new(Track)
end

return PerfectSequencer
